I found the culprit: `Field.contribute_to_class()` unconditionally overwrites any user-defined `get_FIELD_display` on the model. The Django fix is to skip setting the generated method when the class already defines one. Let me apply that change.

I found the culprit: `Field.contribute_to_class()` unconditionally overwrites any user-defined `get_FIELD_display` on the model. The Django fix is to skip setting the generated method when the class already defines one. Let me apply that change.

The fix is complete and verified:

- **Root cause**: `Field.contribute_to_class()` unconditionally set `get_<field>_display` on the model class, clobbering any user-defined override (a behavior change introduced in 2.2).
- **Fix applied**: only generate the method when the class doesn't already define one in its own `__dict__` (matching upstream Django's resolution for this ticket).
- **Verification**: reproduction script passes (direct override respected, inherited override respected on concrete subclasses, generated method still correct for normal/nested/invalid/`None`/empty choice values). `model_fields` (310 tests) and `model_regress` (21 tests) pass fully. The only error in the broader run (`test_unicode_filename`) was confirmed pre-existing on the unpatched baseline via `git stash`.

Nothing further needs changing, so I'll submit.
